headline: Anthropic's debut faded into an ugly reversal that pushed the S&P 500 down 2% to new lows on a six-session losing streak, with VIX near 30, so the AI trade is now being sold regardless of earnings.
regime: Risk-off: S&P -2.0% (-5.5% on five days), Nasdaq -2.2%, Semis ETF -2.6% (-10.8% on five, -18.1% on the month), VIX 29.8 (+54.6% on five). It is the worst stretch since the 2025 tariff shock (609a9937df7e); Anthropic opened 34% above its offer and gave most of it back (b69f76fca650, c1ce285bc9e4). The only relief is the 10-year easing to 5.05% as Treasuries rally (242dbba914eb). Inside AI, cooling is the only segment up on five days (+1.9%, MOD +26.8%) and POWL +12%; compute and neoclouds lost 4.2% on the day.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Senate nears a vote on a landmark permitting bill for transmission (8efe8edf3fa7); Senate passed a bipartisan bill backing nuclear (9fac5c0e55b7)
Constellation beat and raised guidance (65891e147a26); NRG earnings reset the 2027 story (74c271dba9eb); Quanta lifted its dividend 18% (0e649e7580c6)
Cooling +1.9% on five days while Semis fell 10.8%; POWL +12.0%
Against: power_nuclear -11.1% on five days, SMR -20.9%; GEV 34% off its July high despite three guidance raises (7eaa623b93c6)
theses.change_note: +1: the permitting bill and cash-generative IPP beats are real; relative strength of cooling and grid in a crash supports the bottleneck view.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Nvidia raised supply commitments to $390bn, mostly memory (4c63f632edc8); Micron customers lock in supply for years not yet started (7a955d097e46)
Lumentum sales +137% (2e751b1f923c); Keysight beat (a638aa06b38d); AI chip estimates keep rising as prices fall (9bdad13574f9)
Against: 'cracks in the AI capex boom' (f74fd1e23913); US offshore chip rule cuts Alibaba capex (dc310d483b7f)
theses.change_note: Order and supply-commitment data still point up; the selloff is about multiples, not demand. Held at 71.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: CRWV, IREN, NBIS extend the selloff as the Anthropic rally fades (26937d62e218); segment -14.0% on five days, IREN -26.0%
CoreWeave faces supply risk from the Chinese transceiver ban (a003a92a7da1); heavy CRWV trading on financing costs (770254a1ec5b)
Applied Digital down ~71% (ca7eae8eb858); quality gate still drops CRWV, NBIS, IREN, CORZ, CIFR, WULF, APLD
Against: Bernstein keeps Buy on IREN at $55 (a17df8439fd7)
theses.change_note: +2: worst segment again, and a new regulatory supply risk lands on the most levered name.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Nvidia's $390bn of commitments are mostly memory (4c63f632edc8); multi-year DRAM contracts (7a955d097e46); MU reports Dec 17 (26a973b8bb8a)
Memory -0.2% on the day, best segment
Against: TrendForce turns bearish on 2027 NAND prices (6015d47ee7a0), SNDK -19.4% on five days; Whale Rock exits WDC (da5e9359c4cb); ETFs net sellers of MU (d6aece52f2cb)
theses.change_note: DRAM evidence got better and NAND evidence got worse; the thesis now rests on MU/DRAM, not NAND. Held at 43.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Hyperscalers -3.1% on the day, ORCL -13.0% on five days and fails the quality gate
'Cracks in the AI capex boom' commentary (f74fd1e23913)
Against: AMZN only -3.8% on five days; index funds still buying Apple and Microsoft (c012bd255528)
theses.change_note: No new capex or cash-flow data today; held.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: Six-session S&P losing streak, worst since 2025 tariffs (609a9937df7e); Nasdaq new lows after an ugly reversal (c1ce285bc9e4)
Citi stays risk-averse (d1f1765d1b5f); 20 tech stocks down 25-76% from highs (561604389e15); Burry victory lap (6624e5addc42)
VIX 29.8, +54.6% on five days; Semis ETF -18.1% on the month
Against: 10-year eased to 5.05% (242dbba914eb); Tom Lee calls it 'max pain' (d9e944c921f5)
theses.change_note: +3: the IPO-day reversal is a classic distribution signal; a VIX near 30 confirms forced de-risking.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: Chinese optical transceiver ban moves forward despite industry pushback (a003a92a7da1); new offshore AI-chip rule (dc310d483b7f)
Against: Senate nears a landmark permitting bill (8efe8edf3fa7) and passed a bipartisan nuclear bill (9fac5c0e55b7)
theses.change_note: -2: bipartisan permitting and nuclear bills cut against the 'approvals halt' risk, even as trade rules tighten.

theses.title: The Huang probe puts Nvidia, and China export rules, at risk
evidence: Muddy Waters short on Nvidia export compliance (e1c29976ae2d); short seller names Nvidia's former top sales executive in a $2.5bn China chip case (f06ca678980f)
Nvidia ~30% off as the post-Huang sell-off 'gets uglier' (2bd9dd2c7a35, 8761d72594a1); AMD faces similar export allegations (42d04e044479); compute -4.2% on the day
Against: Nvidia still raising supply commitments (4c63f632edc8)
theses.change_note: +5: two short-seller reports and AMD allegations turn yesterday's carried-forward thesis into a live one.

compute.note: -4.2% on the day, -12.1% on five; export short reports hit NVDA and AMD, AVGO held best.

foundry_equipment.note: -10.5% on five days; quality intact, no new order data.

memory_storage.note: Best on the day (-0.2%); DRAM contracts strong, NAND outlook turning down.

networking_optical.note: -12.6% on five days, AAOI -25.3%; LITE growth +136% but transceiver ban adds noise.

servers.note: Raised from underweight: held best on the day (-0.9%) and HPE, JBL, CLS trade at 10-11x forward.

power_nuclear.note: -11.1% on five days, but CEG and NRG beats and nuclear policy support cash-generative IPPs.

grid_electrical.note: -5.5% on five days, POWL +12%; permitting bill is a tailwind.

cooling_thermal.note: Only segment up on five days (+1.9%), MOD +26.8%.

datacenter_neocloud.note: -14.0% on five days, IREN -26%; transceiver ban adds supply risk.

hyperscalers.note: -6.9% on five days, ORCL -13%; AMZN steadiest.

ai_software.note: -20.9% on the month; only cybersecurity (CRWD +5.9%) is bid.

risks: Anthropic breaks its $83 offer and the AI IPO window shuts, extending the sell-off across the chain.
Export-compliance cases widen from Nvidia to AMD and suppliers, with fines or new rules.
VIX near 30 forces further de-leveraging even in quality bottleneck names.
A 5%+ 10-year keeps compressing multiples if the Treasury rally fails.
Neocloud credit stress spreads from equity to bonds and cancels orders upstream.
watch: ANT versus its $83 offer on Friday and whether the S&P breaks its six-day losing streak.
NVDA and AMD response to the short-seller export reports.
Senate vote on the permitting bill and grid/power reaction.
Jacobs Q4 results for data-centre engineering demand (725e39fa1da0).
